title: Beef Birria
subtitle: slow-braised spiced beef, served with broth
excerpt: Beef chuck braised low and slow in a rich, deeply spiced sauce with dried chilli and aromatics. The meat is served with its broth for dipping. This is a slow-weekend project with a spectacular result.
sourceNotes: Birria originates in the state of Jalisco, Mexico, where it was traditionally made with goat meat. Beef versions became popular in Tijuana and spread globally through Mexican diaspora communities.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the meat and broth separately for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead. The flavour deepens overnight in the fridge.

content.text: Toast the whole spices before grinding them -- this makes a noticeable difference to the depth of flavour. Char the onion and garlic in a dry pan before adding them to the braise for a smoky, complex base.

items.prepNote: use 3 dried ancho chillies, soaked and blended
quartered and charred in a dry pan
unpeeled, charred in a dry pan then peeled

content.text: Preheat oven to 160C (fan 140C / gas 3). Season the beef with salt.
Char the quartered onion and whole garlic cloves in a dry frying pan over high heat until blackened on the cut sides. Set aside.
Sear the beef in hot oil in batches until browned all over. Transfer to a deep roasting tin.
Blend the charred onion, peeled garlic, tinned tomatoes, soaked chillies or smoked paprika, cinnamon, cloves, and cumin until smooth.
Pour the blended sauce over the beef. Add the stock, bay leaves, and lime juice. Cover tightly with foil.
Braise in the oven for 2.5 to 3 hours until the beef falls apart when pressed.
Shred the beef. Skim fat from the surface of the broth. Taste the broth and adjust seasoning.
Serve in bowls with broth on the side for dipping. Top with lime juice and fresh coriander.

items.symptom: Beef is still tough after 3 hours
items.cause: Oven too low or beef cut too large
items.fix: Return to the oven for another 30 to 45 minutes. The collagen needs sustained heat to break down.
Add a splash of water to dilute. Add a raw potato piece and simmer for 15 minutes -- it absorbs some salt.

items.cause: Chillies over-soaked or charring went too far
items.fix: Add a little honey or brown sugar to balance the bitterness. Char the onion, not the flesh, next time.

content.text: Birria comes from the state of Jalisco in western Mexico, where it was traditionally made with goat meat at celebrations and family gatherings. Beef versions became widely popular in Tijuana. In recent years, birria tacos dipped in consomme have become one of the most talked-about dishes on social media. The dish has roots going back to the 16th century.
